subject: MSA negotiation: made-whole carve-in for trade-secret/confidentiality — NovaMed
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@novamed.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@novamed.com>, legal@novamed.com
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA redline + confidentiality carve-in request

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the call earlier. Procurement is working to lock the MSA this month; attached is our procurement team's redline (NovaMed_MSA_redline_v2.pdf). Two legal items are blocking sign: (1) explicit uncapped recovery for trade-secret misappropriation and (2) clear evidence-preservation obligations tied to any suspected exfiltration.

High-level ask: if Redwood is responsible for a breach that results in loss or misappropriation of our trade secrets (as defined in Section 2 of the attached), NovaMed needs a "made-whole" remedy uncapped by the liability cap — including reasonable forensic costs, attorneys' fees for preservation, and injunctive relief. For less severe confidentiality incidents (e.g., inadvertent exposure of non-sensitive PII), we're open to the standard liability cap.

We also need a short preservation playbook to attach to the order form so our security team has a checklist if we invoke the carve-in. Please confirm whether Redwood can accept uncapped recovery for willful or grossly negligent theft of trade secrets and provide a draft clause + preservation steps.

Procurement's deadline to present final terms to our CFO is Sept 3, so a quick turn would be appreciated.

Thanks,
Sarah Liu
Sr. Legal Counsel, NovaMed
attachments: NovaMed_MSA_redline_v2.pdf
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@novamed.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA redline + confidentiality carve-in request

Sarah — thanks, received the redline. Looping in Legal (Laura), Sales (Ben) and Security/Compliance (Neha) to align.

Short answer: we understand the ask and it's aligned with customer expectations in high-risk regulated verticals, but we need to narrow the trigger and scope so it's operationally manageable and consistent with our insurance. From an operational perspective we can accept:
- Injunctive relief and equitable remedies outside the cap (standard).
- Reasonable forensic and preservation costs outside the cap where there is credible evidence of intentional misappropriation or willful misconduct.
- For other confidentiality exposures (accidental leaks, configuration mistakes), propose retaining the negotiated liability cap but with a higher sub-cap for data confidentiality incidents.

Questions / asks from our side:
1) Can NovaMed confirm that by "trade secrets" you mean the definition in §2 of your redline (we need the concrete definition to avoid scope creep)?
2) What evidence threshold do you expect before forensic costs become uncapped (e.g., credible indicators of intentional exfiltration such as confirmed exfiltration to external domain + logs)?
3) We'll send a draft clause and a short one-page evidence-preservation checklist — will that satisfy your procurement team?

We want to avoid an unlimited exposure for every confidentiality incident, but are comfortable with a narrowly targeted carve-in for willful theft of trade secrets plus associated preservation/forensic costs. Laura — can you draft up proposed language that protects both parties and preserves the right to injunctive relief?

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai | markus.klein@redwood.ai
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@novamed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Aug 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Draft clause + preservation checklist for trade-secret carve-in

Sarah / team — attaching two files: RWD_proposed_tradesecret_clause.txt (inline language below) and a one-page evidence-preservation-playbook (evidence-preservation-playbook.docx). Please treat as a starting point; happy to iterate quickly.

Proposed insertion (MSA §9.3):
"Notwithstanding Section 9 (Limitation of Liability), the limitation of liability shall not apply to (i) claims for equitable relief (including injunctive relief) and (ii) direct damages and reasonable third-party costs of forensic investigation and evidence preservation reasonably incurred by Customer arising from a confidential information breach that is the result of Redwood's gross negligence, willful misconduct, or intentional misappropriation of Customer's trade secrets. For clarity, this carve-in requires Customer to provide (A) a reasonably specific description of the alleged trade secret at issue, and (B) prima facie indicators of intentional exfiltration or willful misuse (e.g., external exfiltration artifacts, confirmed unauthorized access logs, or other forensic indicators)."

Notes: 
- We added an evidence threshold (prima facie indicators) to limit frivolous invocations.
- We focused uncapped recovery on the narrow set (willful/grossly negligent misappropriation), preserving the core cap for accidental exposures.
- Forensic costs are "reasonable third-party costs" — Redwood asks that any forensic vendor selection be mutually agreed or, if urgent, that Redwood can engage a court-acceptable vendor and present costs with receipts.

Preservation playbook (one-page) includes immediate actions (isolate keys, suspend affected API keys, preserve logs for 90 days, notify designated contacts).

Ben / Neha: any operational comments (RTOs, log retention) before we get this back to NovaMed?

--
Laura Bennett
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Draft clause + preservation checklist for trade-secret carve-in

Laura / Markus — thanks for the quick turnaround and the practical language. Procurement reviewed the draft and the playbook. A few quick points:

1) NovaMed can live with the evidence threshold language so long as the discovery of exfiltration that meets the threshold triggers immediate entitlement to recovery of forensic costs and injunctive relief. We want the clause to be automatic upon meeting the threshold (i.e., not subject to a separate mutual-agreement step).

2) For forensic vendors: we are okay with mutual agreement but given time sensitivity would like a fallback that allows either party to retain a neutral, court-acceptable vendor and present documentation.

3) We need an explicit statement that remedies to "make Customer whole" for trade-secret misappropriation (e.g., recovery of development costs, loss of value reasonably demonstrable) will not be limited by the general liability cap if the threshold is met.

If you can confirm those three points in writing and add the fallback vendor language, procurement will clear the clause and route to CFO for approval by Sept 3. We attached a signed cover memo.

Best regards,
Sarah Liu
Sr. Legal Counsel, NovaMed
attachments: signed-cover-memo.pdf
